question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ orchestration as external-only, or defer until narrower HA/session/runtime trackers settle?
rationale: The gap is real, but the permanent owner boundary crosses core/plugin APIs, config/schema, backend dependencies, worker failure semantics, observability, deployment topology, and security review scope.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad architecture tracker and define the minimal core/plugin API seam before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend.

options.title: Document External Orchestration
options.body: Treat ScalyClaw-style Redis/BullMQ deployments as outside OpenClaw core unless a concrete missing plugin API is identified.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, federation, and runtime ownership issues settle first, then revisit this umbrella when the seams are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad architecture tracker and define the minimal core/plugin API seam before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend.
